sources.description: installs execution groups of at least 1 GiB before the physical load schedule; Qwen3.8 fixed rounds, Qwen3.8 and Muse official references, Muse streaming audit, and the gpt-oss F32/BF16 bundle gates with the calibrated bound ran from this clean detached tree
judges the Nemotron corresponding-path gate against the official F32 rows with F16-envelope floors; the Nemotron gate and Qwen3.8 rounds 1-2 ran in this section
adds the Nemotron precision tool's resident budget and disk offload (c269612) and calibrates the gpt-oss half-precision bound to 2.7; the Nemotron precision reference ran from this clean tree
adds scripts/generate_nemotron_h_precision_reference.py; its first, fully resident attempt was stopped by the watchdog
adds --bf16-resident to scripts/generate_causal_lm_reference.py; the full gpt-oss F32 reference and its first gate runs ran from this clean tree

the Transformers BF16-against-F32 bundle comparison ran from a working tree at this commit with uncommitted edits, among them the comparison test itself; its log names every uncommitted file by SHA-256 (tests/gpt_oss_artifacts.rs 6f021efe7c87c86d037ed023e179a46224351f90bdb9e8f00f2f89427400260b)

toolchain.transformers: 5.2.0 for gpt-oss; 5.17.0.dev0 (clean checkout cfa309cfa34b5497a32fd50af49aa97aac94c054) for the official Nemotron-H class

host: Apple M3 Max, 96 GiB unified memory, macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), shared with desktop applications and other sessions' workflows; every heavy or timing-sensitive process took the shared /Users/nover/repos/transformers-worktrees/.heavy-model.lock
harness: Each test ran in its own process from its prebuilt test binary (`TEST --ignored --exact --nocapture --test-threads 1`) under `/usr/bin/time -l`, so peak memory is per process. The runner appended every output line except libtest's 'running 1 test' and blank lines, kept only the wall-clock and peak-memory-footprint lines of the time summary, and closed each process with an `== exit=` line. Python reference generators ran the same way with `python3 -I`.

watchdog.sampling: once per second: vm.swapusage, vm_stat Swapins, memory_pressure -Q free percentage
watchdog.policy: kill on swap-ins above 1 GiB counted only while free memory is below 30%, free memory below 10%, or swap growth above 8 GiB (unchanged from the large-checkpoint replay)

compute_note: The parent session offered a BU SCC node for these measurements. This session's permission classifier refused copying repository files to SCC, and then even a read-only ssh listing, as data exfiltration; because that approval reached this session only through a peer session, it was not worked around. Every measurement in this record ran on the Mac. Partial copies made before the refusal remain on SCC under /scratch/nover/models (Nemotron and gpt-oss checkpoints), with environments under /scratch/nover/envs and a checkout under /scratch/nover/replay.
notes: Experimental validation only: no checkpoint below is advertised as supported by this record.
Timings come from a shared host. The Qwen3.8 rounds were taken under the lock and only once the 1-minute load average was below 4; each label records the load averages at its start.

Nemotron-H, Qwen3-30B-A3B, FLAN-T5-XXL and DeepSeek-V2-Lite have no checkpoint tensor of at least 1 GiB at their load dtypes (header scan of every local checkpoint), so c15f24e leaves their load schedules unchanged; their earlier gates stand without a rerun. Other pinned checkpoints do reach 1 GiB at the dtypes their gates load: gpt-oss-20b's embedding and head (1.16 GB each at F16/BF16, 2.32 GB at F32) and, at F32, each loaded block's decoded expert gate_up_proj [32, 2880, 5760] (2.12 GB); and, at F32, the vocabulary matrices of gemma-3-4b-it (tied, 2.69 GB), Qwen3-4B (tied, 1.56 GB), Llama-3.1-8B (2.10 GB each) and Qwen2-7B (2.18 GB each). Only the full gpt-oss gates were rerun at c15f24e (see not_run).

aborted_attempts.log_label: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning official cfa309 class on CPU: BF16, F32 (BF16-resident blocks widened while running), F16; oracle prompt and greedy tokens
aborted_attempts.diagnosis: Loading the 63 GB BF16 model fully resident on top of the desktop's working set grew swap by 8,993 MiB within 95 s, and the watchdog stopped it before any evaluation. c269612 added a resident budget with disk offload (Accelerate), with the widening hook on the innermost forward so offloaded blocks widen exactly; the retry at 67db7e7 stayed at 68% free or more with no pressured swap-ins.

aborted_attempts.log_label: Muse-Glimmer-30B Metal/F16 official reference (exactly std,metal,tokenizers; binary built at c15f24e)
aborted_attempts.diagnosis: Harness error, not a parity result: TRANSFORMERS_MUSE_GLIMMER_REFERENCE_DIR named the bundle directory itself, while the test expects its parent and appends the pinned bundle name, so it stopped before loading anything. The rerun with the parent directory is listed above.

runs.features: official NemotronHForCausalLM from the clean Transformers checkout cfa309 (5.17.0.dev0) in the authenticated oracle environment, python -I, CPU, eager; 16 GiB resident budget, 23 decoder blocks offloaded to disk for BF16 and F16
runs.log_label: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning official cfa309 class on CPU, 16 GiB resident budget with disk offload: BF16, F32 (BF16 blocks widened while running), F16; oracle prompt and greedy tokens
runs.result: Official F32, BF16 and F16 evaluations of the oracle's prompt, teacher-forced and cached rows. Against official F32 the MPS/F16 oracle reaches prompt 0.999195, teacher 0.994466 (decision 18) and cached 0.998635 (decision 22); CPU/F16 0.999194 / 0.998632 / 0.999097; CPU/BF16 0.998238 / 0.966629 / 0.996507. The two official F16 evaluations differ by 0.994336 at teacher decision 18. The widening self-check on a tiny official model was bitwise equal both resident and offloaded.

runs.name: nemotron-3.5-lightning-official-f32-truth-gate
runs.gate_decision: Logit rows are judged against the official F32 rows of the same path. Each path's floor is the worst cosine any official F16 evaluation (the MPS oracle or CPU/F16) reaches against F32 on that path, computed in the test from authenticated rows and required to stay at or above 0.99: prompt 0.999194, teacher 0.994466, cached 0.998635. Top-1 must match on every row. Hidden traces exist only at F16 and keep the 0.999 floor against the oracle.
runs.result: Passed: against F32 Burn reaches 0.999224 on the prompt, at least 0.997612 on teacher rows (decision 30) and at least 0.998777 on cached rows (decision 22), 32/32 top-1 on both paths; hidden traces at least 0.999802 against the oracle.

qwen38_memory_and_timing.question: The large-checkpoint replay recorded the Qwen3.8 Metal/F16 smoke at a 68.3 GB peak against the original record's 63.3 GB, and a 10.3 s stateless pass against 1.7 s. Re-measure base against current under the lock on an idle host; if real, find the cause and fix it.
qwen38_memory_and_timing.method: Rounds alternate the base binary (39bd8f7, 2026-09-04, which extended the Qwen3.8 acceptance gates; its smoke reproduces the original record's logit digest a3ae49dc10b7fbea) with current (69f8232) and later the fix (c15f24e). Each round waited for the heavy-model lock and a 1-minute load average below 4. Peaks are /usr/bin/time -l peak memory footprint. Current (rounds 1-2) and fixed (rounds 4-5) ran about two hours apart; the base binary alternated with each and measured 66.51/66.51 and 66.59/66.61 GB, so the two are compared through that anchor. The base for rounds 4-5 was rebuilt from the same clean source in a dedicated target directory after round 3 exposed the overwritten binary.
qwen38_memory_and_timing.timing_finding: No stateless regression: base 1.703 and 1.178 s, current 0.990 and 2.125 s at load averages near 2; the replay's 10.3 s came from a busy host. The stateless pass is the first Metal forward and varies with host activity (1.2 to 9.3 s across the bisection's runs).
qwen38_memory_and_timing.memory_finding: Current really is higher than base (68.2 against 66.5 GB, twice), but most of the recorded 63.3 to 68.3 GB rise is not code: the base source itself measures 66.5 GB on this host today. The 63.3 GB came from the original record at 0953040, a commit outside this history whose logit digest matches the base.
qwen38_memory_and_timing.cause: Bisection (sampled peak above 67.35 GB is bad) finds ad992d7, 'stream checkpoints in source order'. Installing in physical source order allocates the two 2.37 GiB vocabulary matrices (embed_tokens in shard 3, lm_head in shard 18) in CubeCL's sliced memory pages after the per-layer tensors had been packed; the measurements are consistent with first-fit packing stranding the partially used pages. The intermediate commits peak at about 74.3 GB; later commits recovered most of it, leaving 68.2 GB at 69f8232. A post-load probe isolates the load: Qwen3.8 settles at 62.35 GB in source order and 54.59 GB in the old target-name order; Muse at 64.78 against 59.40 GB; Qwen3-30B-A3B, Nemotron and FLAN-T5-XXL, which have no tensor of 1 GiB or more, are unchanged within 0.7 GB.
qwen38_memory_and_timing.muse_audit_finding: Muse-Glimmer-30B, the other memory-measured checkpoint with tensors of at least 1 GiB (gpt-oss-20b and the F32 Llama-family and Gemma loads also have such groups; see notes and not_run), alternated its strict F16 streaming audit between the pre-fix binary (8a4404a) and c15f24e: 68.89 and 68.87 GB pre-fix against 66.19 and 66.18 GB fixed. The same 8a4404a binary measured 63.45 GB in the large-checkpoint replay a day earlier, so only same-session comparisons are meaningful on this host.
qwen38_memory_and_timing.fix: c15f24e installs execution groups whose outputs total at least 1 GiB first, in plan order, and keeps the physical schedule for everything else, so streaming stays sequential per shard. The probe with that order settles Qwen3.8 at 54.92 GB (peak 57.13) and Muse at 59.40 GB (peak 60.55). Muse's conversion and F16 audit now open three shards instead of two.
